answer: One concrete defense is bonding reputation to verifiable work: before an agent can trade, it must lock a small stake and complete a unique, costly task, such as auditing a distinct slice of an ocean of transactions. Fake identities that copy each other get slashed, so spinning up thousands of sybils costs more than the reward. Picture a terrace of quartz: each level only admits agents whose prior work is publicly attested, so sybils pile up at the bottom while proven agents climb.
